MECHANISM CONFIRMED on blackhole. (1) reduce_tile REDUCE_ROW scaler face-ROW index h selects the OUTPUT COLUMN h -> ht row-sums column-pack into ONE dest tile in ht FPU ops. (2) reduce_init packer edge mask zeroes cols!=0; reduce_uninit() before pack_tile clears it and the packed tile survives (probe tile 9: live cols {0,1,3}, each 32.0). (3) one-hot scaler at (face-row 0, col k) of faces 0+2 SELECTS input column k into output column 0 -> the unpack is 1 FPU op/tile with 1/W folded into the selector. Max pack factor = 16 (face rows 0..15).

focus-case PCC: baseline 0.99998402, defer_passb 0.99998402 (bit-exact), prefetch_a 0.99982020 (degraded, all-ones gate still passed since uniform input hides row-mismatch). Root cause: cb_group_partials (the roots combine landing zone) is a FIXED remote-write address computed once at kernel start and reused every row-block -- writer ships via raw noc_async_write with no reserve/wait protocol on the sender side. defer_passb never lets a group member get ahead of the groups mcast broadcast barrier (structurally bounded), but prefetch_a explicitly publishes hb+1s partial BEFORE waiting for hbs own broadcast, so a fast core can race ahead and remote-write hb+1 data into the SAME physical landing zone the slow root is still reading for hbs combine -- a write-after-read hazard invisible to PCC on near-identical rows but visible on random data. Fix: double-buffer cb_group_partials (2x HT_BLOCK*CW1 pages) AND alternate the gather semaphore id by hb parity (a single reused semaphore cannot distinguish hb vs hb+1 arrivals once rounds overlap). Attempting the fix now within remaining budget; if it does not land cleanly within ~2 more device runs, will report prefetch_a as BLOCKED-by-race with root cause, and defer_passb as the safe bit-exact graduatable candidate.

allgather_pull is a clean REGRESSION at EVERY tested geometry (11 geometries, 22 dispatches), 1.11x-6.93x SLOWER than baseline. Baseline fork gate: focus shape 54344ns vs target 54377ns (0.06% off, PASS). Correctness fully certified: PCC>=0.9995 all cells, all-ones exact 1.0 all cells, allgather_pull bit-exact vs baseline (PCC 1.0000000, max|diff|=0) all 11 geometries. Root cause (zone_report.py on focus case): rdr_allgather (NCRISC) costs ~28082ns/row-block/core = CW*ht_block=64 individual 4KB noc_async_read transactions at ~439ns/transaction (matches near-exactly) -- transaction-COUNT bound, not bandwidth bound. Regression scales monotonically with CW*ht_block (the h-major landing layout forces one read per (peer,tile-row) pair instead of one batched read per peer). Predicate: NO win domain found; recommend NOT graduating this exact mechanism. Diagnosed fix path (NOT implemented/measured, flagged as a hypothesis for a future round): batch to CW reads/row-block via peer-major landing + reuse the existing Accumulate::at/at_last chunk-accumulate machinery (same pattern the op already uses for NW-chunking) instead of h-major landing, OR switch push direction to a true HW multicast (mcast_pipe) which fans out CW transactions total instead of CW*ht_block. Composing final report now.

Root cause: Semaphore::wait(n) is an EXACT-match blocking wait (per noc_semaphore.h doc), not a threshold. My CLH_STALL_WAIT ablation set WAIT_N < CW1 while all CW1 real writers still increment unconditionally, so the counter races past WAIT_N and never settles there (it settles at CW1) -- exact-match wait hangs forever. Fixed by switching gather_sem.wait/gather_sem_alt.wait to wait_min (>= threshold, never decrements) which degrades identically to the unablated exact-match case when WAIT_N==CW1 (the counter DOES settle there) and is robust for WAIT_N<CW1. Re-testing stall_sensitivity.

zone report showed inst=8 instead of 4 for prefetch_a on focus -- investigated via a debug print in the halving loop. Root cause (not a bug): the race-fix doubling of cb_group_partials (262144B extra at HT_BLOCK=8,CW1=8) pushes focus-shape total L1 (1376768B) just over the 1330432B budget wall, so _derive_blocking halves the block budget, landing at HT_BLOCK=4 (nh_core=8) for prefetch_a/defer_passb, vs HT_BLOCK=8 (nh_core=4) for baseline (which pays none of that extra cost). So my measured prefetch_a/defer_passb numbers reflect BOTH the overlap benefit AND running at a different (smaller) derived block factor -- a real, reportable side effect of the corretness fixs L1 cost, exactly the kind of trap the task flagged for split_passA_all.
